name: schtasks.exe
description: Adversaries may abuse the Windows Task Scheduler to perform task scheduling for initial or recurring execution of malicious code.
summary: Created a scheduled SYSTEM task that runs when a user logs in
Run malicious scripts on a compromised host (.vbe, .dat)
Downloaded additional malware including Cobalt Strike, PowerShell loader

attack_relationships.description: BRONZE BUTLER has used schtasks to register a scheduled task to execute malware during lateral movement.

Chimera has used scheduled tasks to invoke Cobalt Strike including through batch script schtasks /create /ru "SYSTEM" /tn "update" /tr "cmd /c c:\windows\temp\update.bat" /sc once /f /st and to maintain persistence.
Earth Lusca used the command schtasks /Create /SC ONLOgon /TN WindowsUpdateCheck /TR “[file path]” /ru system for persistence.
Lazarus Group has used schtasks for persistence including through the periodic execution of a remote XSL script or a dropped VBS payload.
Naikon has used schtasks.exe for lateral movement in compromised networks.
Rancor launched a scheduled task to gain persistence using the schtasks /create /sc command.
During C0017, APT41 used `SCHTASKS /Change` to modify legitimate scheduled tasks to run malicious code.

During Operation CuckooBees, the threat actors used scheduled tasks to execute batch scripts for lateral movement with the following command: `SCHTASKS /Create /S <IP Address> /U <Username> /p <Password> /SC ONCE /TN test /TR <Path to a Batch File> /ST <Time> /RU SYSTEM.`

During the SolarWinds Compromise, APT29 used `scheduler` and `schtasks` to create new tasks on remote host as part of their lateral movement. They manipulated scheduled tasks by updating an existing legitimate task to execute their tools and then returned the scheduled task to its original configuration. APT29 also created a scheduled task to maintain SUNSPOT persistence when the host booted.
BADHATCH can use `schtasks.exe` to gain persistence.

CLAIMLOADER has created scheduled tasks that execute the loader every five(5) minutes using `schtasks /F /Create /TN \"<fake_software_name>\" /SC minute /MO 5 /TR
\"C:\ProgramData\<path_to_exe> <hardcoded_argument>\`.
CorKLOG has achieved persistence through the creation of a scheduled task named TableInputServices by using the command `schtasks /create /tn TabletlnputServices /tr /sc minute /mo 10 /f`.

citations.source_name: Zscaler PAKLOG CorkLog SplatCloak Splatdropper April 2025

attack_relationships.description: DEADEYE has used `schtasks /change` to modify scheduled tasks including `\Microsoft\Windows\PLA\Server Manager Performance Monitor`, `\Microsoft\Windows\Ras\ManagerMobility, \Microsoft\Windows\WDI\SrvSetupResults`, and `\Microsoft\Windows\WDI\USOShared`.
Lokibot embedded the commands schtasks /Run /TN \Microsoft\Windows\DiskCleanup\SilentCleanup /I inside a batch script.
Lucifer has established persistence by creating the following scheduled task schtasks /create /sc minute /mo 1 /tn QQMusic ^ /tr C:Users\%USERPROFILE%\Downloads\spread.exe /F.

POWERSTATS has established persistence through a scheduled task using the command ”C:\Windows\system32\schtasks.exe” /Create /F /SC DAILY /ST 12:00 /TN MicrosoftEdge /TR “c:\Windows\system32\wscript.exe C:\Windows\temp\Windows.vbe”.
PUBLOAD has created scheduled tasks to maintain persistence with the command `schtasks.exe /F /Create /TN Microsoft_Licensing /sc minute /MO 1 /TR C:\Users\Public\Libraries\...`

citations.source_name: Cisco Talos MUSTANG PANDA PLUGX PUBLOAD MAY 2022

attack_relationships.description: ServHelper contains modules that will use schtasks to carry out malicious operations.
Tarrask may abuse the Windows schtasks command-line tool to create "hidden" scheduled tasks.

The Gentlemen Ransomware has leveraged scheduled tasks to execute itself as system. The Gentlemen Ransomware has also established persistence through the creation of scheduled tasks to include `schtasks /Create /SC ONSTART /TN UpdateSystem /TR “<malware_path>” /RU SYSTEM` and `schtasks /Create /SC ONSTART /TN UpdateUser /TR “<malware_path>”`. The Gentlemen Ransomware has deleted pre-existing scheduled tasks using `schtasks /Delete /TN UpdateSystem /F` and `schtasks /Delete /TN UpdateUser /F`.
Tomiris has used `SCHTASKS /CREATE /SC DAILY /TN StartDVL /TR "[path to self]" /ST 10:00` to establish persistence.
yty establishes persistence by creating a scheduled task with the command SchTasks /Create /SC DAILY /TN BigData /TR “ + path_file + “/ST 09:30“.
zwShell has used SchTasks for execution.
CSPY Downloader can use the schtasks utility to bypass UAC.

attack_detection_strategies.name: Detection of Suspicious Scheduled Task Creation and Execution on Windows

analytics.description: Detects the creation, modification, or deletion of scheduled tasks through Task Scheduler, WMI, PowerShell, or API-based methods followed by execution from svchost.exe or taskeng.exe. Includes detection of hidden or anomalous scheduled tasks, especially those created under SYSTEM or suspicious user contexts.

analytics.description: Creation or modification of Windows services or scheduled tasks with names or descriptions mimicking legitimate entries, followed by anomalous execution of untrusted binaries or LOLBAS.

related_CVE.description: Windows Task Scheduler elevation of privilege. The public proof of concept runs a legacy Windows XP schtasks.exe (/change /TN bear /RU /RP) against a hard-linked task file to take over a protected file; this is a public exploit, not a documented intrusion.

Netlogon (MS-NRPC) elevation of privilege, known as Zerologon. In a Qbot intrusion where the actors exploited it to get domain admin, Qbot used schtasks.exe to create a task that ran every 30 minutes for persistence.

references.source_name: DFIR Report Qbot and Zerologon February 2022

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.description: Configure the Increase Scheduling Priority option to only allow the Administrators group the rights to schedule a priority process. This can be configured through GPO: Computer Configuration > [Policies] > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Local Policies > User Rights Assignment: Increase scheduling priority.

mitigations.name: Operating System Configuration
mitigations.description: Configure settings for scheduled tasks to force tasks to run under the context of the authenticated account instead of allowing them to run as SYSTEM. The associated Registry key is located at HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\SubmitControl. The setting can be configured through GPO: Computer Configuration > [Policies] > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Local Policies > Security Options: Domain Controller: Allow server operators to schedule tasks, set to disabled.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.description: Limit privileges of user accounts and remediate Privilege Escalation vectors so only authorized administrators can create scheduled tasks on remote systems.

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.description: Toolkits like the PowerSploit framework contain PowerUp modules that can be used to explore systems for permission weaknesses in scheduled tasks that could be used to escalate privileges.
